subject: Where can I find the cdf file for Human Gene 1.0 ST Array

messages.author: 0e2b4a9275e66608
messages.subject: Where can I find the cdf file for Human Gene 1.0 ST Array
parts:
I installed aroma.affymetrix to test its function in exon array
analysis. I downloaded Cel files from Affymetrix (http://
www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/sample_data/gene_1_0_array_data.affx),
however, I couldn't find corresponding cdf file (HuGene-1_0-st-v1)
from http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters.
The Cel files may not be loaded into R with correct cdf file. Could
anyone help me with this problem? It seems that the cdf file can be
found because the Cel data were example data.

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Where can I find the cdf file for Human Gene 1.0 ST Array
parts:
On 26/07/2008, at 12:25 AM, guo wrote:
>
> I installed aroma.affymetrix to test its function in exon array
> analysis. I downloaded Cel files from Affymetrix (http://
> www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/sample_data/gene_1_0_array_data.affx)
> ,
> however, I couldn't find corresponding cdf file (HuGene-1_0-st-v1)
> from http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters
> .
> The Cel files may not be loaded into R with correct cdf file. Could
> anyone help me with this problem? It seems that the cdf file can be
> found because the Cel data were example data.

Hi Xuejiang.

The Affy 'unsupported' CDF can be downloaded from:
http://www.affymetrix.com/Auth/support/downloads/library_files/HuGene-1_0-st-v1.r3.unsupported-cdf.zip

I think that is a text version of the CDF. Before using it within
aroma.affymetrix, you'll want to use 'convertCdf' in the affxparser
package to convert it into the binary version. You can use it from
the text version, but it is *much* faster with the binary version.

I have also created an experimental Ensembl-centric CDF (just by
remapping the probes) for the Gene 1.0 array, which may be of
interest ... you can download it from:
http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/folders/mrobinson/exon/human_cdfs/HuGene-1_0-st-v1_Ensembl47.cdf

Hope that gets you started.

Cheers,
Mark

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Where can I find the cdf file for Human Gene 1.0 ST Array
parts:
Hi,

The reason aroma.affymetrix is complaining is because the CEL header
says that the chip is of type HuGene-1_0-st-v1, but the CDF file has a
different name (HuGene-1_0-st-v1.r3.cdf). Also, your directory
structure does not conform to that expected by the package. Please
see the page at

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/setup

Could you please try the following steps and let us know if you still
experience a problem:

- create a subdirectory HuGene-1_0-st-v1 in annotationData/chipTypes/
- rename your CDF to
annotationData/chipTypes/HuGene-1_0-st-v1/HuGene-1_0-st-v1,r3.cdf
(note the comma in the file name, not a period)
- when you set up the cdf, do: cdf <-
AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuGene-1_0-st-v1", tags="r3")

Cheers,

Ken

Thank you very much for your kind instructions. I modified the names
according to your suggestions and the error disappeared. It seems that
the Cdf file from Affymetrix don't contain gene information. So I used
one compiled by Mark, and the Ensembl gene name were correctly shown
in the results.

Regards,

Karl
